findings.reason: §4 and §5 build the new read on an invariant `push` does not maintain, so the design must either change `push_sprint`'s deliberate hint-not-slot contract or drop the "one pushed sprint" premise the ambiguity decision depends on.
findings.text: the plan asserts the `push` op "promotes and demotes in one versioned write" so "two actives cannot arise from the push op", but `push_sprint` (`reckon/project_state.py:2126-2133`) sets only the target sprint to `active` and its own docstring states the opposite — "`active` marks the sprint being pushed; it is a hint, not an exclusive slot … several sprints may be active at once while several crews work them" — and the write at `:2163` writes `{**target, "status": "active"}` touching no other row. The invariant the plan's active-sprint repair rests on does not exist.

findings.reason: §1's diagnosis and §3's "elected S1/S12" evidence describe a revision that no longer exists, so the plan must be re-measured against the current tree before its repair is scoped.
findings.text: §1 says `read_plan(project, "index")` calls `_derive_default_sprint_focus`, "walks composed order and returns the first sprint holding any unfinished item", and "never reads sprint status at all"; no such symbol exists in `reckon/`, and the reader that does exist, `focus_sprint_id` (`:1251-1284`), first consults the live-crew liveness (`reckon/sprint_liveness.py:225`) then the stored `active` status (`:1270-1279`). The described defect (a closed sprint elected over the pushed one) was landed fixed by commit `bec9f24a7` on 2026-09-25, two days after the plan's measurements, and both surfaces now resolve `active_sprint_id` through this one function (`reckon/project_state.py:1469,1554` and `reckon/roadmap.py:1995`).

findings.reason: the plan should extend `focus_sprint_id`/`sprint_liveness` and the existing audit findings and touch `_has_unfinished_items` for the dangling-item case, rather than authoring a parallel reader that will drift from the owner, as §1's own stale reference to a deleted function already shows.
findings.text: the plan would add a composed read that "must consult stored status rather than walking composed order" (already the behaviour of `focus_sprint_id`, `reckon/project_state.py:1251`), and to make "an unresolvable member slug … reported as a broken reference" the audit already reports it at `reckon/mcp.py:2378` (`sprint-item-missing-plan`) and `reckon/roadmap.py:2305` (`unresolved-sprint-item`). The full census of existing readers/authors of the two facts this plan would re-own: active sprint — `reckon/project_state.py:1216` (`live_sprint_ids`), `:1251` (`focus_sprint_id`), `:1469` and `:1554` (composed `active_sprint_id`), `reckon/roadmap.py:1995` (`_sprint_status_buckets`), `reckon/mcp.py:2301` (audit reads stored `active`); membership — `reckon/roadmap.py:2652-2721` (scalar-vs-items reconciliation, emits `plan-sprint-missing-item`/`-mismatch`), `reckon/mcp.py:2404-2464` (the same in the audit), `reckon/mcp.py:2378` and `reckon/roadmap.py:2305` (unresolvable member already reported), and `reckon/project_state.py:1235-1248` (`_has_unfinished_items`, which still counts a bare slug as unfinished — the one read-path gap the plan names correctly).

findings.reason: against refusal_families 23 the section must account for the added refusal in its own text or justify it, as the interface budget requires.
findings.text: §4 and §5 add a read refusal (the ambiguous-active-sprint read "has no correct answer and must say so rather than choosing") and leave `d-ambiguous-active-sprint` open between refuse and a deterministic pick; it adds to the refusal surface without naming which existing refusal family it retires or merges, or why nothing can be.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the plan adds no module, class or wrapper; it edits existing owners in place, so there is no new surface that could hide behaviour less deeply than what it hides.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan re-implements the active-sprint reader and the membership reconciliation the codebase already owns, at `reckon/project_state.py:1251` and `reckon/mcp.py:2378`.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 1481, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §4 and §5 add a read refusal ("must say so rather than choosing") without naming what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan (measured 2026-09-23) proposes a sprint-focus reader that already exists as `focus_sprint_id` (`reckon/project_state.py:1251`) and the dedicated `reckon` module `reckon/sprint_liveness.py`, and it names `_derive_default_sprint_focus` (`reckon/project_state.py`) which is not in the tree; the plan cites no search of either, and its central invariant premise about the `push` op is contradicted by that op's own docstring.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — no thin layer over existing machinery is proposed; the shape described is an extension of existing readers, so there is no wrapper to justify.
